Who owns, and who invents together

Knowledge made in Europe is not always controlled from Europe, and much of it is made together with partners abroad. For the EP patents on each critical raw material: who owns the inventions made in Europe, which countries invent together, and which organisations file patents jointly.

Invented in Europe, owned elsewhere

Who invents with whom

Share of each row's patents that also have an inventor in the column's country. The diagonal shows the share with inventors only from that country (no partner abroad). Rows need not add up to 100%: a patent can have partners in several countries.

Organisations filing together

Organisations that are joint applicants on this material's patents. Circle size shows their joint patents; colour shows their country. Joint applications are rare (about one patent in eleven), so this shows formal partnerships, not all collaboration. Click a circle to see its partners.

Method

Patents. EP applications filed 2010–2021 in which the material is central (named in the claims, title or abstract, or often in the description); materials with fewer than 300 such patents are left out.

Ownership. A patent's European weight is the share of its inventors in Europe (EU, EFTA and the United Kingdom). That weight is split over the applicants' countries: “owned elsewhere” is the part held by applicants from outside Europe. The reverse direction starts from the share of applicants in Europe and splits it over inventor countries. Inventor and applicant countries from OECD REGPAT, PATSTAT where REGPAT has none.

Co-invention. A patent links every pair of countries in which its inventors live. A multinational filing from its labs in two countries counts as co-invention too.

Joint applicants. PATSTAT harmonised applicant names, cleaned of legal forms; individuals are left out. Per material, up to 50 organisations with at least two joint patents. Name variants of one company may remain separate. Not checked by hand.

Source: EP patents (EPO full text), OECD REGPAT inventors and applicants, PATSTAT harmonised applicant names. Built 2 November 2026 by R/crm_collab_html.R.
